text:
Sometimes love doesn’t change who you are. It creates the safety for who you’ve always been to finally emerge. ❤️

I’ve been experiencing a beautiful transformation recently, and so has someone who has become very dear to me.

For much of my life, I lived heavily in my masculine energy. Not because I rejected my feminine nature, but because circumstances required me to be the protector, the provider, the problem solver, the one who held everything together.

Survival became a way of living.

And somewhere beneath all that strength was a woman who simply wanted to laugh more. To be playful. To have deep conversations without someone feeling threatened by her thoughts. To sing, dance, create, and enjoy the moment without wondering what might come crashing down next.

I never stopped being that woman.

I just didn’t always have the space to let her breathe.

And then I met Nate.

What has unfolded between us has been remarkable, not because either of us arrived to rescue the other, but because we’ve discovered something neither of us had consistently experienced before.

The freedom to be completely ourselves in another person’s presence.

Nate has known his own share of difficult beginnings. He learned very young that joy could feel unsafe, that being carefree might leave him vulnerable to whatever came next.

And recently he said something that touched me deeply.

“You allow me to be so joyous, and I don’t have to be afraid about what’s coming next.”

And I realized we’re experiencing two sides of the same transformation.

He gives me room to soften.

I give him room to play.

He encourages the woman who no longer wants to carry everything alone.

I encourage the curious, creative, joyful man who doesn’t have to suppress his excitement or wonder whether he’s being too much.

We laugh. We explore ridiculous rabbit holes. We have conversations that wander everywhere. We challenge one another without turning differences into threats.

And neither of us has to wear a mask.

That is the teaching I want to share.

So many of us have spent years adapting to environments where being fully ourselves didn’t feel safe.

We became serious.

Hyperindependent.

Guarded.

Responsible for everyone and everything.

We confused our survival adaptations with our personalities.

But sometimes, when we encounter another being who genuinely sees us, hears us, respects us, and supports our sovereignty, something extraordinary happens.

The parts of ourselves we tucked away begin to return.

The inner child remembers how to play.

The nervous system begins learning that connection doesn’t always have to come with danger.

And love stops feeling like something we must earn through sacrifice.

Whether you call that connection a soulmate, twin flame, chosen flame, or simply two people who recognize something beautiful in one another, the label matters far less than the experience.

Can you be yourself?

Can you laugh without being judged?

Can you disagree without fearing abandonment?

Can you be vulnerable without having that vulnerability used against you?

Can you experience joy without waiting for the other shoe to drop?

And can you offer that same freedom in return?

Because this isn’t about finding someone to complete you.

It’s about two people who have done their own inner work creating a relationship where neither has to disappear to keep the connection.

These days, I wake up, make my coffee, and find myself smiling before the day has even begun.

Not because life has suddenly become perfect.

But because I know I can show up exactly as I am.

No performance.

No armor.

No mask.

Just me.

And after a lifetime of learning how to survive, the freedom to simply live, laugh, love, and be fully seen is a gift beyond measure.

I share because I know I’m not the only one ❤️‍🔥

LFG — Love, Forgiveness & Gratitude.

 Evariel 🐉❤️

I wrote this a couple of years ago when Christmas for me became something painful... I can say with great thanks that it hasn't REMAINED painful like this since... my children will wake up in my new home on Christmas morning... I even hope my ex and her new husband find the time to stop by. But I wanted to repost and add this : if you are struggling this Christmas and need someone to talk to... reach out. DM me. Let's talk...

Christmas Morning, 2023

I am going to share a bit of pain this morning... don't feel a need to read or respond. Just putting this out there.

This is the first Christmas morning I have ever, in my entire life, spent alone. I have felt a lot of pain in my life... that's not to say that I am more a man of sorrows than any other and I am blessed beyond belief in so many ways. But I woke up to a quiet house this Christmas morning. No kids running down the stairs to see what awaited them. No coffee brewing. No one to make breakfast for. No one to sit with on the couch and watch the mayhem... and the lights in the eyes of people I love. I can say with complete certainty that I have never felt more what it means to be alone than right now...

There is a real weight to pain and sadness. As men, we're expected to shut it down. Keep it inside. Fight it silently and on our own. And honestly, when my kids DO get to my place later this morning, I don't think I can allow them to see this pain. I need them to know Christmas is still Christmas. It is a time for peace on Earth and goodwill toward men. That a savior was born for them... not just to save them from an eternity that would... let's just say... not be optimal, but to save them in the here and now. To offer them hope in their darkest of circumstances. To be a personal God who understands everything they've ever felt or ever will and offers them love and comfort in that pain, but also forgiveness for the thoughts that may come in the depths of that same pain. I need them to know that their father believes in that salvation... and trusts it.

But I am struggling this morning to feel that 'salvation'... I am struggling to not drown in self-pity... to not feel and think deeply bad things. And while all that is true, and to some degree makes me feel like a failure, I know that I am really NOT struggling alone and I know that there will come a better morning. And that even if that morning is not Christmas morning, it really still is. Every day can be a celebration of what Christ has done and is doing for us.
I look forward to that day…

text:
This clip is from the Adiyogi Alayam consecration ceremony conducted by Sadhguru (Jaggi Vasudev) at the Isha Yoga Center near Coimbatore on December 24, 2011. In the footage, he mixes milk from a black cow (kara pasu) with what he states is venom from a black cobra, swallows a small amount from his palm, and then pours the remainder from the same flask onto the Linga.

1. The Toxicology: Why Swallowing Venom Usually Doesn't Kill

 In toxicology, there is a strict distinction between a poison (absorbed via ingestion, inhalation, or skin contact) and a venom (designed to be injected directly into tissue or the bloodstream):
 * Digestion destroys venom proteins: Cobra venom consists primarily of large, complex proteins and peptides—most notably postsynaptic \alpha-neurotoxins (such as cobratoxin) and digestive enzymes. Because these molecules are fragile proteins, hydrochloric acid (\text{HCl}) in the stomach and proteolytic enzymes (pepsin, trypsin, and chymotrypsin) rapidly denature and break them down into harmless amino acids, much like dietary protein.
 * Black cow milk adds no chemical protection: Milk has no antivenom or neutralizing properties against snake toxins; it merely dilutes the liquid volume.
 * Why it remains genuinely risky: Even without active ulcers, swallowing venom is not risk-free. Micro-abrasions from brushing teeth, bleeding gums, minor esophagitis, or silent gastritis can provide a direct gateway into the bloodstream. Accidentally aspirating even a microscopic droplet into the lungs also bypasses digestive enzymes and allows immediate absorption into circulation. Furthermore, in India, procuring or handling venom from protected species like the Indian cobra (Naja naja) falls under strict prohibitions of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.

2. The Ritual Perspective: Ucchishta vs. Tantric Symbolism

Whether applying the remaining mixture to the Linga constitutes blasphemy depends entirely on which Hindu framework is being applied:

 * Orthodox Agamic and Vedic rules: In mainstream temple traditions, your objection aligns directly with strict ritual purity (shaucham) laws. Any substance that has come into contact with human saliva or been consumed first is classified as ucchishta (contaminated leftover) and is strictly forbidden from being offered to a deity or used in abhishekam. Under standard Agama codes, pouring a personal concoction onto a Linga after tasting from the same container is a clear violation of sanctity.

 * Non-Agamic / Tantric framing: Consecration rituals (Prana Pratishtha) claimed to follow Tantric or Siddha lineages deliberately operate outside conventional temple Agama purity rules. In this framing, the combination of cobra venom and milk invokes Shaiva iconography—specifically Shiva as Neelakantha (who holds poison in his throat) and Nageshwara (adorned with a cobra)—while treating the practitioner's body as part of an energetic transmutation rather than an ordinary vessel subject to ucchishta taboos.
Because this footage circulates online without context, it routinely draws criticism from two opposite directions: rationalists who point out that digesting protein-based venom is basic human physiology & a stunt to impress gullible people rather than a miraculous feat, and traditional Hindus who view offering ucchishta substances to a Shiva Linga as sacrilegious.

Think & form your own conclusions.

Biblical Illiteracy & the Self-Salvation Trap: A Shadow-to-Substance Study
When nominal Christians walk away from the faith—or trade the cross of Christ for a works-based religion—it is rarely because they examined Scripture and found it wanting. It happens because institutional Christianity traded rigorous exposition for shallow entertainment, leaving millions spiritually defenseless. Yet in an age where every lexicon, manuscript, and cross-reference sits at our fingertips, ignorance is no longer a victimhood—it is a choice.
1. The Shadow: Priestly Neglect & the Lost Book of the Law (2 Kings 22; Hosea 4:6)
A Temple Without the Text (2 Kings 22:8–13): Under centuries of apostate kings in Judah, the Book of the Law (sēper hattôrāh) was literally lost inside the temple itself. Religious routines continued, yet God’s people had no idea what the covenant actually commanded or warned—until Hilkiah found the scroll and Josiah tore his clothes upon hearing the primary text read aloud.
The Covenant Indictment (Hosea 4:6; Amos 8:11): God did not blame pagan nations for Israel’s collapse; He indicted the spiritual shepherds first ("My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from being a priest to me"), followed by a judicial famine—not of bread, "but of hearing the words of the Lord."
The Fatal Error of Self-Righteousness (Isa. 64:6; Rom. 10:2–3): Whenever people lose sight of God’s absolute holiness and the sacrificial blood required to approach Him (Lev. 17:11), they inevitably invent a scale of human works—attempting to establish their own righteousness rather than submitting to God’s.
2. The Substance: Zero Excuses & the Only Sufficient Mediator (Acts 17:11; Hebrews 9–10)
Individual Accountability in the Light (Luke 12:48; Acts 17:11): Under the New Covenant, God has placed the complete written canon in the hands of His people and indwelt believers with the Spirit of truth (John 16:13). Luke commends the Bereans not for trusting religious credentials, but for examining the Scriptures daily (anakrinontes tas graphas) to verify whether even apostolic preaching aligned with the text.
Why Works-Based Religions Always Fail the Plumbline (Gal. 2:21; Heb. 9:22): Every human religion built on moral self-improvement, dietary rules, and scales of good deeds collapses on one foundational reality: "without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness of sins" (Heb. 9:22). Finite, fallen creatures cannot pay an infinite moral debt to a perfectly holy God—"if righteousness were through the law, then Christ died for no purpose" (Gal. 2:21).
The Sinless Divine-Human Mediator (1 Tim. 2:5; Heb. 7:25–27): Because no mere prophet, angel, or ritual can bridge the gulf between a holy Creator and guilty sinners, the eternal Son took on human flesh (John 1:1, 14), lived the sinless obedience we failed to live, and offered Himself once for all on the cross—rendering every rival system obsolete (Heb. 10:12–14).
3. The Plumbline for Today
Stop Outsourcing Your Faith: A neglected Bible on the shelf and a steady diet of shallow Sunday soundbites will leave any household vulnerable to deception. Read the primary text for yourself and verify every claim against its plain grammar and context (2 Tim. 2:15).
Refuse the "Scales of Deeds" Illusion: Any system that tells you your good works can outweigh your sin lowers the holiness of God and denies the necessity of the cross. True peace comes solely through the finished atonement of Christ (Rom. 5:1).
High Access Means High Accountability: Never in history have seekers had fewer excuses for biblical illiteracy. With the full canon and neutral linguistic tools immediately available, refusing to search out the truth is no longer lack of access—it is lack of appetite.

Fr Robinson,
You have taken several true statements and used them to defend a false one. That is not careful theology. It is rhetorical sleight of hand.
Our Lord was a Jew. Not in some vague cultural sense, and not merely because our Saviour was born in Judea. Our Redeemer was a Jew according to the flesh, by descent, by covenant, and by the clear testimony of Scripture. Yahweh incarnate was “of the seed of David according to the flesh” (Romans 1:3). Our Lord descended from Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Judah (Matthew 1; Hebrews 7:14). Our Saviour was circumcised on the eighth day, presented in the temple according to the Law of Moses, and lived under that Law (Luke 2:21–24; Galatians 4:4). Our Redeemer taught in the synagogues, kept the feasts, and identified Himself with Israel’s covenants and promises. Our Lord said, “Salvation is from the Jews” (John 4:22). The Gospels present Yahweh in the flesh as the Messiah of Israel—the Son of David, the Lion of the tribe of Judah.

To deny that is to deny the text. You cannot erase the Jewishness of our Saviour without erasing the historical reality of the Incarnation. 

God the Son took on human nature in a specific people, in a specific lineage, at a specific moment in redemptive history. That is not optional background. It is essential to the gospel.

You are correct that our Lord was not a Talmudic Jew. The Talmud as we know it did not yet exist. You are correct that our Redeemer fulfilled the Law and the Prophets and thereby brought the old sacrificial system to an end (Matthew 5:17). The veil was torn. The temple was destroyed, just as our Saviour predicted. The Levitical priesthood is finished. Animal sacrifices are obsolete because the final sacrifice has been offered by Yahweh in the flesh. And modern Judaism, like the Judaism that rejected our Lord in the first century, is a system that refuses its own Messiah and therefore has no saving power.
None of that justifies the claim that “Jesus was not a Jew.” That is an overstatement that collapses categories the New Testament keeps distinct.

You are also wrong on the larger issue of Israel and the Church. “Not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel” (Romans 9:6) is true—true Israel has always been defined by faith, not mere ethnicity. But Romans 11 is equally clear: God has not rejected His people. A partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in, and then “all Israel will be saved” (Romans 11:25–26). That is not a reference to the Church. The Church does not replace Israel. The gifts and calling of God are irrevocable. Gentiles are grafted in; they do not displace the root.

Finally, your appeal to “the perpetual sacrifice of the Mass” and a continuing sacerdotal priesthood is a different and more serious error. 

Our Redeemer offered Himself once for all (Hebrews 7:27; 9:12, 26; 10:10–14). To speak of re-presenting or perpetuating that sacrifice is to contradict the finished work of the cross. That is not a minor difference of emphasis. It is another gospel.

So let the record be clear. Modern Judaism rejects the Messiah and cannot save. The Church is the people of God, composed of believing Jews and Gentiles. There is neither Jew nor Greek in Christ for justification. But our Lord was a Jew according to the flesh. The promises were given to Israel. And those realities are not negotiable if we are going to handle the Word of God accurately.

With all due respect, Calvin, the issue is not what you think. What does our Lord say?

3、中韩先开盘，日本要多等一个美国交易日。

1、エヌビディア固有のリスクが、関連株の評価にも波及しうる。
エヌビディアは14.01％安。ロイターは関係者2人の話として、SECが潜在的な会計上の問題を調べていると報じた。違反が認定されたという報道ではない。中国のAIインフラ、日本の半導体製造装置、韓国のメモリーには評価面の圧力が及ぶ可能性がある。実際の受注変化は別途確認したい。

2、米国債が買われても、株安は止まらなかった。
米財務省の日次10年債利回りは5.04％から4.92％へ低下。金利低下は株価評価を支えうるが、同時に株式に求められるリスクプレミアムが上がる場合もある。アジアの輸出企業では、金利とともに受注の見通しや業績予想を確認する必要がある。

3、日本の休場が、情報を織り込む順番を変える。

2、국채가 올라도 주식은 큰 폭으로 하락했다.
미 재무부의 일별 10년물 금리는 5.04%에서 4.92%로 내려갔다. 금리 하락이 주가 평가에 도움이 될 수 있지만, 투자자가 요구하는 주식 위험 보상도 동시에 커질 수 있다. 아시아 수출기업은 금리와 함께 수주 가시성, 실적 가이던스를 확인할 필요가 있다.

3、중국·한국과 일본의 가격 반영 시점이 다르다.

Theo tôi, cổ phiếu hạ tầng AI Trung Quốc, thiết bị bán dẫn Nhật Bản và bộ nhớ Hàn Quốc có thể chịu sức ép định giá. Đơn hàng thực tế thay đổi ra sao vẫn cần bằng chứng riêng.

2、Trái phiếu tăng giá nhưng chưa bảo vệ được cổ phiếu.
Lợi suất chuẩn kỳ hạn 10 năm do Bộ Tài chính Mỹ công bố hằng ngày giảm từ 5,04% xuống 4,92%. 3、Các thị trường châu Á sẽ phản ánh thông tin theo lịch khác nhau.
